diet.text: Snakes, rodents, lizards, birds and carrion

overview.text: The Cape Cobra is a highly venomous cobra of southern Africa, living in dry savanna, fynbos, bushveld and desert.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually about 1.2 to 1.4 m, up to 1.6 m; the record is 1.88 m. Males are slightly bigger.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Western and central South Africa, southern Namibia, south-western Botswana and western Lesotho.

behaviour.text: Active by day, rarely at night. It lives on the ground but climbs trees and bushes well, for example to raid nests. Birds of prey and honey badgers hunt it.

diet.text: Eats almost anything it can catch: other snakes, rodents, lizards, birds - and even carrion.
